reader.requirement: At --std 85 the space (and, in reference format, the line end) is a separator wherever the formats need one, any run of spaces is accepted where one separator space is, the spaces after a comma, semicolon or period belong to that separator, and two character-strings with no separator between them are one character-string.
reader.edition-search: Read the WS, FNARG_SEPARATOR, DOT, COMMA and SEMICOLON lexer rules and SeparatorRule.cs whole (its remarks state it is edition-invariant); grepped Edition|Version|Std in SeparatorRule.cs and PictureSeparatorPeriodRule.cs (none) and read Frontend.cs LexAndParse: the edition reaches the lexer only through retypes.PrimeLexer (reserved-word retyping) and the debugging-line rewriter, neither of which touches WS or the [,;]-space separator.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c17_separator_spaces covers runs of spaces and spaces after comma/semicolon/period in procedure statements; not data-division entries, division/section headers, or the refusal (character-strings with no separator)

probes.printed: A=007007! / B=Q / C=BCD / D=016 / E / F (EXPECT: MATCH)
probes.expected: runs of spaces between every word of headers, data entries, subscripts, reference modifiers, arithmetic and conditions, and before periods, all accepted with unchanged meaning

probes.printed: COBOL5506: missing token before 'TON-B' ... expected TO
probes.expected: TO and N-B with no separator form one character-string TON-B, so MOVE has no TO: refused

probes.printed: COBOL2632 the period is not followed by a space
probes.expected: a period with no space after it is no separator

reader.notes: The lexer skips [ \n]+ as one WS token and the [,;]-plus-spaces as one separator token, so the spaces after a comma or semicolon are consumed with it exactly as SR1's last sentence says. The same lexer serves every edition.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 aimed inside list regions and the text-manipulation path, which the reader did not try: s1 runs of spaces after a comma and a semicolon inside subscripts W-F (2,    1) W-F (2;    2), a comma at line end inside a subscript, FUNCTION MAX (3,    7,     5) and (3   9   5), W-T (2:   3): A=C B=D C=E D=07 E=09 F=BCD, all right; s2 COPY with runs of spaces and pseudo-text ==MOVE    1== against library text MOVE 1: LIB=07 (multiple spaces matched as one separator); s3 REPLACE ==MOVE    1,   TO== matched MOVE 1 TO and MOVE 1 <line end> TO: R=08 S=08. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR1.
